_comment: SPARK — S161 W1-B castle atlas specs, one entry per RACE, consumed by scripts/build-sprite-atlas.mjs.
RETAINED IN-TREE for the same reason design-spec.json is: S151 shipped three atlases and kept no
spec, so they could not be rebuilt or retuned.
⭐ `framesPerState: 1` AND `still` INSTEAD OF `clip`. A castle has three CONDITIONS, not three
ACTIONS — see the `still` knob's docblock in build-sprite-atlas.mjs for why that is not a
shortcut. Each state is therefore a one-frame row and `ticksPerFrame` is inert; it is set to 1
rather than omitted because the manifest schema is shared with the animated characters and a
missing key there would read as a builder bug rather than as a deliberate constant.
⛔ `fit: 'box'` AND NOT THE DEFAULT `'height'`, WHICH IS THE ONE JUDGEMENT CALL IN THIS FILE.
Height-fit exists because CHARACTERS are compared by how tall they look, and it lets a prop
widen the cell (the archer's bow). Castles are not compared that way: they sit at FIXED anchors,
they are a click target sized KEEP_W x KEEP_H, and the six differ enormously in aspect —
measured on the shipped art, the vampire spire is 622x976 and the naga reef fort is 979x806.
Height-fitting those two makes the naga nearly a third wider than the board slot while the
vampire stays narrow. Box-fit puts every race inside the SAME square and lets each keep its own
aspect: a spire is tall and thin, a reef fort is wide and squat, and neither overruns its seat.
The union bbox is measured per ATLAS, so a race's three states share one ground line and one
scale — an intact keep and its own ruin cannot jump. It does NOT span races, which is exactly
why the square cell above matters: it is what keeps six separately-built atlases comparable.
_white_limit: ⛔ enclosedWhiteLimitPct 4e-05 — S165, after the owner spotted white patches: "some of them have
that white background because not cut out too well" and "look at the tower cut out and destroction
video some of them still have some white backgrounds small parts too". He was right on both.
THE CAUSE WAS AN OMISSION, NOT A TUNING ERROR: these specs never set the knob at all, so they took
build-sprite-atlas.mjs's DEFAULT of 0.003 — which is 75x more permissive than the 4e-05 the race
units were tuned to in S164. Enclosed near-white BELOW the limit is deliberately KEPT (that is what
saves eyes and blade glints), so a loose limit ships background pockets as opaque white blobs.
⭐ MEASURED, AND THE METRIC THAT MATTERS IS LARGEST POCKET, NOT TOTAL. At 4e-05 the units carry
66-768 px of near-white in TOTAL but their biggest single pocket is 2-52 px — eye glints, correctly
kept. The castles and towers at 0.003 had biggest pockets of 113-168 px, which is a visible patch.
⭐ AND AN AGGRESSIVE LIMIT IS SAFER ON A STRUCTURE THAN ON A CHARACTER. A character has eyes and
teeth to protect, which is the whole reason the knob exists and why the orc needed its own value.
sharedStyle here already forbids anything white or near-white ON the building, so by construction
every near-white pocket in one of these frames is background.
